correctness.rationale: All vertices of I_{n,k} are 0–1 vectors with at most k ones; the Gaussian support selects at most k largest positive coordinates, so the lost cube width is exactly the sum of the (B−k)_+ smallest positives plus the (n−B−k)_+ smallest absolute negatives, divided by ||G||. Width equality requires n−k≤B≤k (Gaussian sign count), giving the exact finite binomial identity even when the range is empty. For each sign group b~n/2, transform half-normal order statistics using uniforms and exponential spacings; maximal-inequality and F^−1(u)=u/a+O(u²) show Σ_{j≤m}X_(j)=m²/(2ba)+o_P(1) uniformly for m≤Ksqrt(n). Binomial CLT for B and Gaussian radius normalization give Q_c(Z). The ordinary cube width expands by the delta method to Y of variance 1−3/π, and signs are exactly independent of absolute magnitudes, yielding asymptotic independence. At c=0, Q=χ_1²/(4a); c>0 atom mass 2Φ(2c)−1, c≤0 none. Independently enumerated 525 small-n vertex-support tests (n=2..8) confirm the finite identity; no finite test purports to prove CLT.
